q-48243.name: Question 1
q-48243.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14262965/assets/69d48bb02c5c0e7552b4ff9dd5fb7db1c91422f5b60d864f3ac7ca60f194b56f.png)

On which of the following intervals is the function $y=f(x)$ above continuous? You may assume that all points of discontinuity of $f(x)$ are shown in the diagram.
q-48243.worked_solution:
To determine the intervals of continuity of a function, we take the domain of the function and exclude any points of discontinuity.

The function is defined on the interval $(-\infty ,\infty ).$ There is a discontinuity at $x=2,$ so we need to exclude this point. 

Therefore, the function is continuous on the intervals $(-\infty ,2)$ and $(2,\infty ).$  It is also continuous on any subinterval of these intervals.

Among the answer choices, the correct one is the following:

$\,$ $(2,\infty )$ 

Notice that:

- The intervals $(0,\infty ),$  $(-2,4),$  $(-\infty ,6),$  and $(1,\infty )$ contain the excluded point $x=2,$ so the function is not continuous on any of these  these intervals.

Question 1

On which of the following intervals is the function y=f(x) above continuous? You may assume that all points of discontinuity of f(x) are shown in the diagram.

a
 (0,∞)
b
 (−2,4)
c
(−∞,6)
d
 (1,∞)
e
 (2,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To determine the intervals of continuity of a function, we take the domain of the function and exclude any points of discontinuity.

The function is defined on the interval (−∞,∞). There is a discontinuity at x=2, so we need to exclude this point.

Therefore, the function is continuous on the intervals (−∞,2) and (2,∞). It is also continuous on any subinterval of these intervals.

Among the answer choices, the correct one is the following:

(2,∞)

Notice that:

  • The intervals (0,∞), (−2,4), (−∞,6), and (1,∞) contain the excluded point x=2, so the function is not continuous on any of these these intervals.

q-104891.name: Question 3
q-104891.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14262965/assets/69fd9e95c75086b7cd4d027c13ff2bbbdf0e543579115cc1151e1e3febbcd732.png)

On which of the following intervals is the function $y=f(x)$ above continuous?
q-104891.worked_solution:
The function is continuous on the open intervals $(-\infty ,-2),$ $(-2,2)$ and $(2,\infty ).$

Additionally, the function is right-continuous at $x=-2$ and left-continuous at $x=2.$ Hence, it is continuous on the closed interval $[-2,2].$

Therefore, we can say that the function is continuous on the intervals $(-\infty ,-2),$ $[-2,2]$ and $(2,\infty ).$ It is also continuous on any subinterval of these intervals.

Among the answer choices, the correct one is the following:

$\,$ $[-1,2]$ 

Notice that

- $[-3,-1]$ and $[-10,0]$ contain the point of discontinuity $x=-2,$ so the function is not continuous on these intervals.

- $[0,5]$ and $[1,3]$ contain the point of discontinuity $x=2,$ so the function is not continuous on these intervals.

q-104891.html:
Question 3
?

On which of the following intervals is the function y=f(x) above continuous?

a
[−1,2]
b
[−10,0]
c
[−3,−1]
d
[1,3]
e
[0,5]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The function is continuous on the open intervals (−∞,−2), (−2,2) and (2,∞).

Additionally, the function is right-continuous at x=−2 and left-continuous at x=2. Hence, it is continuous on the closed interval [−2,2].

Therefore, we can say that the function is continuous on the intervals (−∞,−2), [−2,2] and (2,∞). It is also continuous on any subinterval of these intervals.

Among the answer choices, the correct one is the following:

[−1,2]

Notice that

  • [−3,−1] and [−10,0] contain the point of discontinuity x=−2, so the function is not continuous on these intervals.

  • [0,5] and [1,3] contain the point of discontinuity x=2, so the function is not continuous on these intervals.

q-104893.name: Question 4
q-104893.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14262965/assets/8f0677c0a29729be721c0a7528377c646a222f5404c69ea8dc6ba941f70bc5f2.png)

On which of the following intervals is the function $y=f(x)$ above continuous?
q-104893.worked_solution:
The function is continuous on the open intervals  $(-3,0),$  $(0,1)$ and $(1,4).$

Additionally, the function is right-continuous at $x=-3$ and left-continuous at $x=0.$ 

Therefore, we can say that the function is continuous on the intervals $[-3,0],$  $(0,1)$ and $(1,4).$ It is also continuous on any subinterval of these intervals.

Among the answer choices, the correct one is the following:

$\,$ $[-2,-1]$ 

Notice that

- $[1,2]$ and $[1,3]$ contain the endpoint $x=1,$ but the function is not right-continuous at this point.

- $[-1,1]$ contains the point of discontinuity $x=0,$ so the function is not continuous on this interval.

- $[2,4]$  contains the endpoint $x=4,$ but the function is not left-continuous at this point.

Among the answer choices, the correct one is the following:

  • [−1,1] contains the point of discontinuity x=0, so the function is not continuous on this interval.

  • [2,4] contains the endpoint x=4, but the function is not left-continuous at this point.
